article.story: SYRACUSE, N.Y. -- — Abdramane Siby scored a season-high 17 points off the bench, Ryan Moesch had a near triple-double, and Syracuse dominated the second half on the way to a 74-53 victory over Albany on Wednesday night. Siby, a 7-foot freshman from Mali, went 8 for 8 from the field and made 1 of 4 free throws. He has made all 14 of his shots this season. Moesch had 13 points, nine rebounds and eight assists. He also had four steals. Sadiq White Jr. had 10 points and 11 rebounds for the Orange (5-2). The score was tied at 26 at halftime and Syracuse went up by 10 about 8 1/2 minutes into the second half. The Orange took control with a 14-0 run that left them with a 68-43 lead with 5 1/2 minutes left in the game. Siby scored 14 points in the second half and his 7-for-7 shooting helped Syracuse to 63% from the field after halftime. Syracuse shot 48% for the game and held Albany to 30%. Syracuse led 8-2 in the early going but that would be the largest lead for the Orange until a dunk by Siby made it 45-37 with 12 1/2 minutes left in the game. Ollie Engen scored 23 points and Pedro Santos 14 for the Great Danes (4-5). Up next Syracuse: The Orange play at Oklahoma on Tuesday in the SEC/ACC Challenge. Albany: The Great Danes visit Penn State on Tuesday. -------- Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here.
